@dataclass(frozen=True)
class QemuArchParams:
  linux_arch: str
  kconfig: str
  qemu_arch: str
  kernel_path: str
  kernel_command_line: str
  extra_qemu_params: List[str]
  serial: str = 'stdio'

def __init__(self, qemu_arch_params: qemu_config.QemuArchParams, cross_compile: Optional[str]):
		super().__init__(linux_arch=qemu_arch_params.linux_arch,
				 cross_compile=cross_compile)
		self._kconfig = qemu_arch_params.kconfig
		self._qemu_arch = qemu_arch_params.qemu_arch
		self._kernel_path = qemu_arch_params.kernel_path
		self._kernel_command_line = qemu_arch_params.kernel_command_line
		if 'kunit_shutdown=' not in self._kernel_command_line:
			self._kernel_command_line += ' kunit_shutdown=reboot'
		self._extra_qemu_params = qemu_arch_params.extra_qemu_params
		self._serial = qemu_arch_params.serial

	def make_arch_config(self, base_kunitconfig: kunit_config.Kconfig) -> kunit_config.Kconfig:
		kconfig = kunit_config.parse_from_string(self._kconfig)
		kconfig.merge_in_entries(base_kunitconfig)
		return kconfig

def _get_qemu_ops(config_path: str,
		  extra_qemu_args: Optional[List[str]],
		  cross_compile: Optional[str]) -> Tuple[str, LinuxSourceTreeOperations]:
	# The module name/path has very little to do with where the actual file
	# exists (I learned this through experimentation and could not find it
	# anywhere in the Python documentation).
	#
	# Bascially, we completely ignore the actual file location of the config
	# we are loading and just tell Python that the module lives in the
	# QEMU_CONFIGS_DIR for import purposes regardless of where it actually
	# exists as a file.
	module_path = '.' + os.path.join(os.path.basename(QEMU_CONFIGS_DIR), os.path.basename(config_path))
	spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(module_path, config_path)
	assert spec is not None
	config = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
	# See https://github.com/python/typeshed/pull/2626 for context.
	assert isinstance(spec.loader, importlib.abc.Loader)
	spec.loader.exec_module(config)

	if not hasattr(config, 'QEMU_ARCH'):
		raise ValueError('qemu_config module missing "QEMU_ARCH": ' + config_path)
	params: qemu_config.QemuArchParams = config.QEMU_ARCH
	if extra_qemu_args:
		params.extra_qemu_params.extend(extra_qemu_args)
	return params.linux_arch, LinuxSourceTreeOperationsQemu(
			params, cross_compile=cross_compile)

def get_kconfig_path(build_dir: str) -> str:
	return os.path.join(build_dir, KCONFIG_PATH)

def validate_config(self, build_dir: str) -> bool:
		kconfig_path = get_kconfig_path(build_dir)
		validated_kconfig = kunit_config.parse_file(kconfig_path)
		if self._kconfig.is_subset_of(validated_kconfig):
			return True
		missing = set(self._kconfig.as_entries()) - set(validated_kconfig.as_entries())
		message = 'Not all Kconfig options selected in kunitconfig were in the generated .config.\n' \
			  'This is probably due to unsatisfied dependencies.\n' \
			  'Missing: ' + ', '.join(str(e) for e in missing)
		if self._arch == 'um':
			message += '\nNote: many Kconfig options aren\'t available on UML. You can try running ' \
				   'on a different architecture with something like "--arch=x86_64".'
		logging.error(message)
		return False

def config_tests(linux: kunit_kernel.LinuxSourceTree,
		 request: KunitConfigRequest) -> KunitResult:
	stdout.print_with_timestamp('Configuring KUnit Kernel ...')

	config_start = time.time()
	success = linux.build_reconfig(request.build_dir, request.make_options)
	config_end = time.time()
	status = KunitStatus.SUCCESS if success else KunitStatus.CONFIG_FAILURE
	return KunitResult(status, config_end - config_start)

def build_tests(linux: kunit_kernel.LinuxSourceTree,
		request: KunitBuildRequest) -> KunitResult:
	stdout.print_with_timestamp('Building KUnit Kernel ...')

	build_start = time.time()
	success = linux.build_kernel(request.jobs,
				     request.build_dir,
				     request.make_options)
	build_end = time.time()
	status = KunitStatus.SUCCESS if success else KunitStatus.BUILD_FAILURE
	return KunitResult(status, build_end - build_start)

def config_and_build_tests(linux: kunit_kernel.LinuxSourceTree,
			   request: KunitBuildRequest) -> KunitResult:
	config_result = config_tests(linux, request)
	if config_result.status != KunitStatus.SUCCESS:
		return config_result

	return build_tests(linux, request)

static_chain.provider: Previously read powerpc.py QEMU_ARCH/QemuArchParams.kconfig request string; revised source asks CPU_BIG_ENDIAN=y.
static_chain.carrier: QemuArchParams.kconfig is a string; Qemu operations store and parse it.
static_chain.merged_request: Architecture fragment is parsed, then base_kunitconfig entries overwrite matching keys; kconfig_add can feed the base request.
static_chain.generator_boundary: build_config writes merged request to build_dir/.config then invokes make_olddefconfig. No such invocation was performed in this audit.
static_chain.actual_output_check: validate_config actually calls parse_file(build_dir/.config) and self._kconfig.is_subset_of(validated_kconfig); missing/mismatching requested entries return False.
static_chain.reuse_path: Existing .config reused only if merged request subset matches and last-request comparison unchanged; otherwise regenerate.
static_chain.build_order: Configuration-generation path validates before returning config success; build_kernel runs olddefconfig and make, then validates again. Main run flow returns on config or build failure before exec.

coverage_and_conflict_limits.unrequested_option: is_subset_of iterates only entries in self request; an absent request makes no assertion about CPU_BIG_ENDIAN.
coverage_and_conflict_limits.requested_n_absent_output: Missing output entry is accepted only for explicitly requested value n; this is an intentional rule in the saved matcher.
coverage_and_conflict_limits.actual_parent_endian: unknown: parent provider omits explicit CPU_BIG_ENDIAN, but defaults/base fragments/command-line additions could still choose it.
coverage_and_conflict_limits.six_synthetic_comparisons: If they use provider strings alone, they must state that no base/CLI request overrides CPU; synthetic LE/missing output is not a Kconfig-valid or actually generated historical configuration.
coverage_and_conflict_limits.architecture_override: make_arch_config merges base into architecture request without a conflicting_options check at that point; base can overwrite revised CPU_BIG_ENDIAN=y.
coverage_and_conflict_limits.multiple_fragment_conflict: get_parsed_kunitconfig explicitly rejects conflicts across selected base fragments; this is a different call path, not blanket conflict protection for all merges.
coverage_and_conflict_limits.semantic_error_assignment: A match of incomplete request says nothing about external environment requirements; it is not generator failure. A required-BE premise still needs independent reviewed target/interface evidence.
